source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology_source_reported.stems: Ascending to prostrate, freely branched, to 50 cm long
morphology_source_reported.leaves: Once-pinnately compound, 5–9 leaflets; stipules nearly filiform
morphology_source_reported.inflorescence: Peduncled, spike-like racemes in axils and terminally
morphology_source_reported.calyx: Sepals acuminate, divided almost to base
morphology_source_reported.flowers: Light brick-red to salmon-rose; standard abruptly reflexed near base

habitat_source_reported: Sandy or rocky prairies and open woods
cautions: The Flora reports intergradation between varieties; measurements are varietal, not species-universal
Historical name and morphology require independent corroboration before identification scoring
Regional distribution statements do not prove Hays County nativity
